question.problem: It is known that $40%$ of a given population have blood type O$+.$ What is the variance of the number of people in a random sample of $100$ people having blood type O$+?$
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of people having blood type O$+.$

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=100$ people

- the probability of finding a person with blood type O$+$ is $p=40%=0.4$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(100,0.4).$

For a binomial random variable $X,$ the variance is given by

$$
\text{Var}[X]=np(1-p),
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

So, the variance of the number of people with blood type O$+$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =np(1-p) \\  & =(100)(0.4)(1-0.4) \\  & =(40)(0.6) \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$
